narrative: Fire dominated today's batch: multi-decadal evidence from the Pantanal shows a fire regime shift toward longer seasons and larger burns since 2014, while a review of Australia's Black Summer response shows biodiversity-focused emergency interventions can work alongside protecting lives and property. Climate signals ran throughout, from European mountain flora showing surprising resilience behind microrefugia to a global meta-analysis finding urbanisation consistently makes wildlife bolder and more exploratory. Movement research traced how migratory red deer redistribute nitrogen across Alpine landscapes and how jaguar connectivity remains strong in South America but badly fragmented further north. On trophic and community fronts, invasive fish were shown to disrupt size-spectrum relationships in freshwater systems, mycorrhizal fungi emerged as reciprocal carbon-nitrogen conduits in grassland, and a new superposition method promises faster food-web reconstruction from isotope data. Restoration studies delivered encouraging news, with rewetted temperate fens converging toward near-natural vegetation after decades and subalpine forests recovering similar carbon stocks via different mycorrhizal pathways. Methodological advances clustered around bioacoustic monitoring, with new evolutionary algorithms and contrastive learning approaches promising faster, less labour-intensive species detection from soundscapes.
